definitions.explanation: Used in conversation to express strong agreement or to confirm what someone has said. Often signals that the speaker has just remembered or recognized something.

examples.japanese: 「{昨日|きのう}のニュース{見|み}た？」「そうそう、{驚|おどろ}いたよね。」
examples.english: "Did you see yesterday's news?" "Yeah, I was surprised."

examples.japanese: そうそう、{言|い}い{忘|わす}れてたけど、{来週|らいしゅう}の{予定|よてい}が{変|か}わったよ。
examples.english: Oh right, I forgot to mention — next week's plans have changed.

notes:
USAGE:
そうそう serves two main conversational functions:
1. Enthusiastic agreement — confirming what someone just said, stronger than a single そう
2. Recollection — introducing something the speaker just remembered, similar to "oh right" or "speaking of which"

The repetition of そう adds emphasis and casualness. In polite conversation, a single そうですね would be preferred.
